text:
Leo Carlsson's third season looks like the one Anaheim drafted him second overall for. He is playing 20:15 a night, up more than a minute, and he is on the ice for 89% of the Ducks' power-play time. That is where the points live: 18 of his 26 come with the extra man, and his 26 points in 18 games are a big jump from 0.96 a game last season.

Some of it will settle. His scoring rate of 4.28 points per 60 runs well above our talent range of roughly 2.7 to 3.6, and he is converting 20% of his shots on just 30 attempts on net. The underlying style is the real part: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 73% of his entries and among the top setup men in the league, and Evolving-Hockey said his chances last season were better than his goals.

Watch the even-strength share. If he starts adding five-on-five points to the power-play haul, the 98-point projection stops looking generous.
headline: Carlsson has the Ducks' power play humming
